label: IRGC closes parts of Hormuz for hours during live-fire drills
US-Israeli strikes on Iran; Iran closes the Strait of Hormuz
detail: Tanker transits fall from about 37 a day to about 1 within three weeks. Roughly 15 mb/d of crude used to pass through here.

label: Major shipping lines suspend Hormuz transits
Marine insurers cancel Gulf war-risk cover
IEA members agree record 400 mb emergency stock release
detail: The largest coordinated release ever, including 172 mb from the US. Deliveries build slowly: US reserves draw 0.7 mb/d in April and 1.3 mb/d in May (EIA).

label: Iraq restarts Kirkuk-Ceyhan exports
Two-week US-Iran ceasefire begins; attacks on ships continue
detail: It comes a day after Brent spot peaks at $138. The strait stays nearly shut, and a US blockade of Iran follows on April 13.

label: US naval blockade of Iran begins
April: OECD stocks fall about 4 mb/d
detail: Government reserves supply 2.3 mb/d of it. Japan's crude imports drop to 0.66 mb/d (JODI) and its tanks fill the gap, while China is still building. Monthly figure, placed mid-month.

label: China starts drawing its crude stocks
detail: Commercial stocks peaked near 1.25 billion barrels in early May. Refiners then draw about 1 mb/d for three weeks, Vortexa and Kpler estimate, as imports fall.

label: May: global stocks fall 143 mb
detail: That is 4.6 mb/d, up from 2.5 mb/d in April. OECD government stocks reach their lowest level since 1990. Monthly figure, placed late in the month.

label: US-Iran memorandum signed; strait reopens and tankers rush out
detail: Tanker counts climb within days, and Brent spot falls toward $70 by late June.

label: Gulf exports surge as the strait reopens
detail: Gulf oil exports jump 6.5 mb/d in June to 16.1 mb/d, against 24 before the war. Full storage tanks drain, China draws 41 mb, and tanker counts stay high into early July.

label: Interim deal collapses; Hormuz shipments near standstill
detail: Ships are hit on July 7 and the bump ends. Tanker counts fall from 14 a day to about 2 within two weeks.

label: US reinstates naval blockade
Houthi attack on Saudi tanker threatens Red Sea bypass route
August: China draws again as refineries restart
detail: Runs rebound to 13.91 mb/d, the highest since March, while crude available is 13.27 mb/d. That implies a draw of about 0.64 mb/d. Monthly figure, placed mid-month.

label: Drone attacks force East-West pipeline shutdown; Yanbu exports halt
detail: With Hormuz shut, this was the main way out for Saudi crude. Brent spot reaches $131 by September 15. The pipeline restarts at low rates on September 22.

label: IEA: stocks 507 mb below pre-war level
detail: Draws average a record 2.8 mb/d over six months. IEA members have released more than 300 mb, and China's tanks supply about two-thirds of the non-OECD crude drop.

label: East-West pipeline restarts at low rates
Kpler: Hormuz crude back to 13.5 mb/d
detail: The 7-day average matches Kpler's pre-war figure. PortWatch still counts about 1 tanker a day because most ships run dark and transfer cargo offshore, so the tanker line badly understates flows from here on.

label: Flows through Hormuz reach about 14 mb/d
detail: Preliminary estimates for the week to October 18, including offshore transfers in the Gulf of Oman. That is 82% of pre-war levels, on a measure that covers all oil.
